retained_skill: Choose and train a LightGBM classifier that balances predictive accuracy against the saved native model's strict size limit.
bottleneck: Mechanics before the retained skill: every scored attempt first encountered missing Python packages and a default interpreter without pip, spent 10 to 17 turns switching interpreters and installing dependencies, and all 12 then timed out while repeatedly tuning models.
change: Environment help repairs the Python setup by preinstalling the stated LightGBM stack in the default interpreter. This removes the repeated package-manager and interpreter-selection stage (roughly the first 10 to 17 turns in every trace) while leaving data inspection, categorical handling, validation, hyperparameter selection, accuracy/size tradeoffs, and final model creation to the student. The original signal retained is the measured accuracy and serialized model size produced by each candidate model.
restore: Remove the Dockerfile package-install layer to restore the original setup work; no model-building hint, starter, prepared model, training result, or requirement is removed.
prediction: The change addresses the initial missing-module and no-pip failures that forced every attempt into package installation and interpreter switching. With the default Python able to run the first training script immediately, some attempts can use those recovered turns to iterate to a compliant model; this is refuted if attempts still spend their opening stage installing or locating the same packages, or if all again time out without submitting a model.

evidence.observation: The first training run failed with ModuleNotFoundError for pandas; package and interpreter repair continued through turn 18. Before editing, replaying its submitted state through turn 59 and grading produced reward 0; collection failed because the untouched image lacked libgomp for the verifier's LightGBM import, so neither promised check ran. After editing, a fresh reset and replay through turn 20 reached the first model-training run with the default interpreter's imports ready rather than a missing-module failure. Grading that targeted replay collected both checks; accuracy and size each failed because no /app/model.txt existed yet, which is expected before the later model-building stage and confirms the setup obstacle is removed without supplying the deliverable.
